title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a manuscript statement headed 'Th' (theorem). It is written on the back of an unrelated administrative typescript.

**Setting.** Let E_∞ be the category of locally compact Hausdorff spaces that are 'locally conical everywhere, including at infinity'. This means each point, and the point ∞ of the one-point compactification X̂, has a neighbourhood that is an open cone on a compact 'link'.

**Claim.** On E_∞ there are two Z-valued invariants: χ, the ordinary Euler characteristic, and χ_!, the Euler characteristic with compact supports. They satisfy:
- (a) χ_! = χ on compact (proper) spaces.
- (b) Cut-and-paste additivity of χ_!: χ_!(X) = χ_!(Y) + χ_!(X∖Y) for Y closed in X.
- (c) Mayer–Vietoris for χ on closed covers: χ(X) = χ(X') + χ(X'') − χ(X'∩X'').
- (d) χ is a homotopy invariant and χ_! is a homeomorphism invariant. The image shows two different equivalence symbols.
- (e) χ(pt) = 1.
- (f) Both are multiplicative on products.
- (g) Both are multiplicative in locally trivial fibrations, χ(X) = χ(Y)χ(F) and χ_!(X) = χ_!(Y)χ_!(F). This is asserted at least when the base Y is a 'relative polyhedron' (a difference of two polyhedra, one linearly embedded in the other). A margin note says: 'I don't know if it is true without such a restriction.'
- (h) With X̂ the one-point compactification (also in E_∞):
  - χ_!(X) = χ(X̂) − 1;
  - χ(X) − χ_!(X) = χ(S), where S is the 'boundary at infinity', i.e. the link of ∞.

**Check of (h).** Write X̂ = X ∪ (cone on S) glued along S×(0,1). Mayer–Vietoris gives χ(X̂) = χ(X) + 1 − χ(S). Combined with the first formula this gives the second. Examples:
- X = R: 1 − (−1) = 2 = χ(S⁰).
- X = Rⁿ: 1 − (−1)ⁿ = χ(Sⁿ⁻¹).

**Final assertion.** On relative polyhedra, χ and χ_! are uniquely determined by (a)–(e). For a cellular filtration, χ_!(X) = Σ(−1)^i f_i, where f_i counts the open i-cells (the 'Euler formula'). A second margin note says: 'I don't know whether χ, χ_! are characterized by a)–e) on all of E_∞.'

**Interpretation.** In modern terms this is an axiomatization of the Euler characteristic as the unique additive (cut-and-paste) invariant on a 'tame' class of spaces. It relates to the ordinary χ through the link at infinity, and it poses the uniqueness and fibration-multiplicativity questions for the whole tame category. The archival context (Gauss–Manin/Cartier file, [1972]–1981) gives no visible link to that topic. Its natural home is Grothendieck's later 'topologie modérée' (Esquisse, 1984) and the χ_c-versus-χ comparison theme (SGA 5; Laumon 1981 in ℓ-adic cohomology).
errors: (c) as written omits the hypothesis X = X' ∪ X''. As stated (any two closed subsets) it is false; it is clearly the intended Mayer–Vietoris for a closed cover.

(d) The machine transcription uses the same symbol twice. For χ_! the equivalence must be a homeomorphism (or proper homotopy equivalence), since χ_! is not homotopy invariant: χ_!(R) = −1 while χ_!(pt) = 1. The image does show two different symbols.

(g) The polyhedral restriction is unnecessary for χ_!. Leray with compact supports, Rf_! applied to the locally constant sheaves H^q_c(F), gives multiplicativity once the base has finite-dimensional compactly supported cohomology for local systems; this holds for this tame class. For χ, multiplicativity likewise follows from Serre/Leray with local coefficients over a base of finite homotopy type. Grothendieck's doubt is overly cautious rather than an error.
(h) The second formula requires the conical structure at ∞, which is built into E_∞. For compact X, S is empty and the formulas degenerate correctly.

ideas.what: Compactly supported Euler characteristic χ_! as a cut-and-paste additive, multiplicative invariant, versus ordinary χ as homotopy invariant satisfying Mayer–Vietoris
ideas.modern_name: Euler characteristic with compact supports / Euler characteristic as valuation (Euler calculus)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Euler–Poincaré, Hadwiger for valuations). Systematized by Viro (1988), Schapira (1991), Schanuel (1991), van den Dries (1998, o-minimal)
ideas.where_published: χ_c versus χ for étale cohomology appears in the SGA 4–5 circle (Grothendieck–Illusie; Laumon 1981 proves χ_c = χ). This topological axiomatization is not known to me in his published texts.

ideas.what: χ(X) − χ_!(X) = χ(link at infinity), and χ_!(X) = χ(X̂) − 1
ideas.modern_name: Euler characteristic of the link at infinity; one-point compactification formula
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; standard in stratified/o-minimal topology (e.g. Euler integration literature)

ideas.what: Uniqueness of χ, χ_! from the axioms on a 'tame' category of locally conical spaces, with the cell-count formula χ_! = Σ(−1)^i f_i
ideas.modern_name: χ_c as the universal additive invariant: Grothendieck ring of definable sets ≅ Z
ideas.usually_credited_to: van den Dries (1998, Tame Topology and o-minimal structures); Krajíček–Scanlon (2000); Schanuel (1991)
ideas.where_published: The spirit of 'topologie modérée' is in Esquisse d'un programme §5 (1984), but not this Euler-characteristic statement, as far as I know.

ideas.what: Category of locally compact spaces that are locally conical everywhere, including at infinity, as the natural domain for these invariants
ideas.modern_name: Locally cone-like / CS-sets (Siebenmann 1972); tame (o-minimal, stratified) topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Siebenmann (1972); Thom–Mather stratification theory; o-minimality (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly poses whether (a)–(e) characterize χ and χ_! on the whole locally conical category E_∞, not just on relative polyhedra. He also asks whether fibration-multiplicativity holds without polyhedral restrictions on the base. The first is essentially the question of the Grothendieck ring of a tame topological category. That question was later answered for o-minimal/definable sets (K_0 ≅ Z via χ_c), but not for the purely topological locally-conical class, which contains non-triangulable spaces.
missed.quote: j'ignore si χ et χ_! sont caractérisés par a) à e) sur tout E_∞
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early, pre-Esquisse formulation of 'tame topology plus universal additive invariant'. It documents that Grothendieck was thinking of Euler characteristics as Grothendieck-ring-type invariants on a tame category, which is of historical interest for the genesis of topologie modérée. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (axioms for χ and χ_c, the link-at-infinity formula, cell-count uniqueness) is classical or folklore and later systematized in o-minimal geometry and Euler calculus. The modest interest is historical: an explicit early axiomatization on a 'locally conical including at ∞' category, with the uniqueness question left open, prefiguring the tame-topology programme of the Esquisse.

'de compactifié[?] X̂' reads more plausibly as 'de sorte que X̂ ∈ E_∞'. X̂ is the one-point (Alexandroff) compactification.
'frontière[?] à l'infini' is confirmed in sense: S is the link/boundary at infinity.
